summary: Ask for the card: take a ticket, an application's place in the coordinator's line. `class` says whether the work is needed now (`responsive`, the default) or can wait (`scheduled`). Waiting tickets are offered the card responsive first, then scheduled, and first come, first served within a class; nothing is ever taken from a holder. `models` is what the application wants to run on the card: each model's key, the engine that runs it, and the memory it needs, `null` while the application cannot say. What they need together, and the margin the coordinator keeps free beside it (`limits.margin_mib` on `/state`), is checked against the card before the card is theirs: an ask that could never fit - more than the whole card - is refused at once, whatever its class, `never_fits`, saying the numbers (`memory`) and taking no ticket; whether it fits NOW is decided when the ticket claims the card (`/card/claim`). The answer is the ticket and its secret `token`. This is the only answer that carries the token, and the coordinator keeps only its sha256: a ticket is acted on with its token alone, so no other application can wait on it, claim it, renew it, release it or cancel it. A ticket asked of a free card with nobody ahead is `offered` at once; any other is `waiting`, and its asker then waits on it (`/card/wait`), never asking again. Every answer is about the asker's own ticket and nothing else: never who holds the card, what runs on it, or who else waits. `holder` is what the asker calls itself, `actor` who it is; `label` is a word for the operator; `for` names the request the ticket serves, so the record can join a rental to the work it was for. SCHEDULED WORK (S18, the owner's second ruling of 2026-09-28): `if_no_room` says what a scheduled ticket does when its models do not fit at its claim - `wait`, the default: it waits in line for room, passed over, and is offered the card again once they fit, its `room` saying the numbers it waits on (what is needed, what is free, what programs outside the bootstrap hold, and when the card was read); or `fail`: it is refused at once, `no_room`, in the loud words a responsive ticket is. `not_before` is the time - seconds since the epoch, as every other time here - it starts no earlier than: until then it is in line and holds back nobody - never offered the card, and never counted as another ticket wanting it - and at its time it is offered the card like any other, the first moment it is free; a time already past is now, and the time is looked at on the coordinator's clock on every beat, so a machine that slept through it is offered it when it wakes. Responsive work is now: it always fails at once when it does not fit, so a responsive ask that names `if_no_room: wait`, or a `not_before` still to come, is refused `live_is_now`, and so is a `not_before` that is not a finite number, `bad_request`. Every ticket says its `not_before` (null: none), its `if_no_room` (`fail` for responsive work) and its `room` (null until it is passed over).

examples.name: the card is free and nobody is ahead: offered at once
the card is held: waiting, and told nothing of who has it
a batch planned in the morning for tonight: in line, not before its time, holding back nobody until then
scheduled work that would rather fail than wait for room
live work at a time still to come: refused, live is now

response.error: live work is now: a responsive ticket starts at once or not at all, so it names no time still to come (not_before 1790204400 is 32388 s away); ask it as scheduled work to plan it for later
